title: Screen Recording Too Quiet on iPhone? How to Make It Louder
description: iPhone screen recordings often come out too quiet. Learn why, how to record louder next time, and how to boost an existing recording 10× with Increase Volume.
h1: How to make a screen recording louder on iPhone
card_summary: iOS captures app audio at a low level. Fix a finished recording in one minute and record louder next time.
quick_answer: A finished iPhone screen recording cannot be made louder with system settings, but you can boost the file: open it in Increase Volume, drag the Volume multiplication slider to ×5–×10, tap Boost Volume, check the Processed version and tap Download Processed. To record louder next time, raise the in-app media volume before you start, disconnect Bluetooth headphones, and long-press the record button to enable the microphone for narration.
intro: Screen recordings are the quietest videos most iPhones ever produce. iOS captures app audio at a conservative level to avoid distortion, and if your headphones were connected or the app's own volume was low, the captured track can be almost silent. Add a voice-over through the microphone and the mix gets even more uneven.
Below: the reasons your recording is quiet, what to change before the next one, and how to rescue the recording you already have.

sections.heading: Why iPhone screen recordings are so quiet
paragraphs: Four causes account for almost every case:
list: Capture level: iOS records internal app audio at a reduced level so loud games and videos do not clip.
Bluetooth: when AirPods or a Bluetooth speaker are connected, captured audio is often much quieter or missing entirely.
In-app volume: the recording captures the app's audio at the volume you had set. If the phone was at 30%, the recording is at 30%.
Microphone mix: if you enabled the microphone, your voice and the app audio are mixed, and iOS lowers the app audio to make room.

sections.heading: Record louder next time
paragraphs: Before you tap record: disconnect Bluetooth audio, turn the media volume up to maximum, and mute notifications with a Focus mode. If you want narration, long-press the Screen Recording button in Control Center and tap Microphone so it turns red; a plain tap records app audio only. A five-second test recording tells you within seconds whether the level is right.

sections.heading: Fix the recording you already have
paragraphs: System settings cannot change a file that is already saved. iMovie can raise it to about 500%, which is sometimes enough but requires building a project and re-exporting. Increase Volume goes to ×10, works directly on the file from Photos, and shows an Original/Processed toggle so you can hear the boosted level before saving. For tutorials with speech, switch on Improve Audio Quality to make the voice easier to understand.

steps.heading: Step by step: boost a screen recording
steps.intro: You need the free Increase Volume app and the screen recording in Photos.

items.name: Share the recording to the app
items.text: Open the screen recording in Photos, tap Share and choose Increase Volume. Or open the app and add the file from Photos.

items.name: Turn on Improve Audio Quality for narration
items.text: If you talked over the recording, enable the Improve Audio Quality toggle so speech stays clear when boosted.

items.name: Set the multiplier
items.text: Drag Volume multiplication to ×5 as a starting point. Screen recordings are usually far below normal level, so ×8–×10 is common. Tap Boost Volume.

items.name: Listen to Processed
items.text: Flip to Processed and play the loudest part of the recording. If it sounds harsh, step the multiplier down.

items.name: Download Processed
items.text: Tap Download Processed and choose Save Video to add the louder recording to Photos, or send it straight to YouTube, Slack, Messages or your editor.

tips.heading: Tips
items: Boost before you trim or add captions in another editor; a louder source gives every downstream tool more to work with.
For gameplay recordings with music, a moderate boost (×3–×4) keeps the music from clipping while lifting the overall level.
If the recording is silent rather than quiet, the audio was never captured (usually a muted app or a DRM-protected video). No booster can add sound that was not recorded.

faq.question: Why does my iPhone screen recording have no sound at all?
faq.answer: Either the app you recorded pauses its audio when it detects screen recording (streaming and video-call apps do this), or the video was DRM-protected, or the phone's media volume was at zero. A silent track cannot be boosted; re-record with the app's audio playing and volume up.

faq.question: Can I make the microphone narration louder but not the game audio?
faq.answer: Increase Volume boosts the mixed track as a whole. Turning on Improve Audio Quality favours speech intelligibility, which usually makes narration stand out more after the boost.

faq.question: Does boosting change the video resolution?
faq.answer: No. Only the audio track is processed; the picture is passed through.
